venue.name: Milner Gardens and Woodland
venue.description: Milner Gardens and Woodland is a 70 acre garden and coastal forest estate on the shore at Qualicum Beach, owned and run by Vancouver Island University. The grounds hold old growth Douglas firs and cedars, a large collection of rare rhododendrons, a food garden, natural ponds and the historic Milner House, which contains the Camellia Tea Room. Its children's education programme, Shoots with Roots, is planned and led by a certified teacher and takes school classes and community groups for single field trips or for a free year long series of five visits. The garden opens to the public on a seasonal timetable that changes month by month, and it is closed in November and January.
venue.address: 2179 Island Hwy W, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1G1

facility_notes.washrooms: Accessible washrooms can be found at the Welcome and Interpretive Centre, Pool House Gift Shop and Milner House. Most of our washrooms are private and gender neutral. There are gendered washrooms with stalls in Milner House. We rarely visit these washrooms with school groups or day camps.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The Welcome Centre, teaching shelter, and our indoor classroom space are wheelchair accessible. Our trails are a mixture of hard-packed gravel, wooden plank boardwalks, and woodchip trails. We have wheelchair accessible gardening planters in our Food Garden. There are some areas, such as rock paths, steps, and lawns, that may require wheelchair users to take an alternate route. We do our best to use wheelchair accessible routes for the whole group during school programs.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: A 6 or 8 person shuttle cart is available to transport guests from the Welcome and Interpretive Centre down to Milner House and back. It can accommodate collapsible wheelchairs, walkers and strollers on the back. The Milner property is a long, gentle slope of trails and roadways that some guests with wheelchairs, walkers or strollers may find challenging to push back up.
facility_notes.rain_backup: Our programs run rain or shine. Please discuss appropriate clothing and footwear with your students. We may cancel a program on the rare occasion that extreme weather such as high winds or heavy snow presents a safety risk.

restrictions: No pets are permitted on the grounds except for certified guide dogs.
The harvesting/cutting of any plant material for consuming, selling or personal use is not permitted. All plants and what they may produce are property of Milner Gardens & Woodland.
Smoking is only permitted in the designated smoking area outside the Pool House Gift Shop.
Garden admission is cut off 30 minutes before closing. We recommend giving yourself at least one hour in the Gardens.
Payment of admission is required to access Milner House, the Camellia Tea Room, the Plant Sales Nursery, and the Pool House Gift Shop.
The Welcome Centre accepts cash, debit and credit. Plant Sales, Pool House Gift Shop and Camellia Tea Room take debit/credit only, no cash. AMEX is not accepted anywhere onsite.
venue.hours_notes: In September the garden is open Thursdays to Sundays, 11 am to 5 pm, with last entry at 4:30 pm. From October 2 it drops to Fridays and Saturdays, 11 am to 3:30 pm, with last entry at 3 pm. It closes for November, opens again on Fridays and Saturdays from mid February, and runs Thursdays to Sundays from April through September. January is closed.
venue.seasonal_notes: Opening days, hours and admission all change month by month. Adult admission is $7 in March, February and October, $10 in April and September, and $14 from May through August. Youth is $5, $6 or $10 to match, and children aged 12 and under are always free, as are Milner members and VIU students and alumni. Between May and September there is often a wedding on site, and parts of Milner House and the Grand Lawn may be closed to the public that day.
venue.price_year_or_season: Admission rates read from their 2026 seasonal pages on 7 September 2026. The December listing on their winter page still shows the 2025 Christmas Magic dates, so that one has passed. The $200 field trip fee carries no year on the page.

programs.name: Shoots with Roots field trip
programs.description: A single visit field trip of two and a half hours for one class or a community group, led by the Shoots with Roots coordinator and adapted to the ages and abilities of the group. There are five themes on the menu. Nature Observers, Junior Gardeners and Pollinators are offered for all ages. Birding for Beginners and Plant Detectives are for grade 3 and up. Pollinators runs in April and May only, the rest from April through August. The fee is $200 for the whole group rather than per student, and the maximum is one class, or 30 students for a community group. Field trips normally run on Thursdays and Fridays, and the page says other days can sometimes be squeezed in.
programs.what_children_do: Move around the forest, garden and natural ponds doing short hands on sensory activities, then get guided exploration time at their own pace. Depending on the theme they may water the food garden, plant seeds in newspaper pots to take home, dig soil and pull weeds, count birds for a list that gets uploaded afterwards, or pollinate flowers themselves with paintbrushes.
programs.our_note: The $200 covers the whole group, so a class of 28 costs the same as a class of 12. Two of the five themes are written for grade 3 and up, so say the age of your children when you email and let them pick. Ask early about days other than Thursday and Friday, because they say they can sometimes fit you in.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site and accessible, and most are private and gender neutral. Staff say they keep the whole group on step free routes during school programs. Nothing is published about where a group eats or where a bus parks, so ask when you book.
programs.evidence: $200 per group. Maximum group size is one class, or 30 students for community groups.

programs.name: Shoots with Roots Five Visit Program
programs.description: A year long series of five field trips for one class, designed and led by the Shoots with Roots coordinator, a certified teacher with a master's in special education. The visits run soil in September or October, trees in October or November, signs of spring in February or March, pollination in April or May, and a reflection and celebration visit in May or June. Grades 1 to 3 have priority in the application process and grades 1 to 7, including K and 1 classes, are encouraged to apply for the spaces left over. Visits are Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday mornings from 9:30 to noon and are all scheduled in early September. Each class may bring a maximum of three adults including the teacher, plus any extra adult a particular student needs. The programme is free, paid for by donors rather than by school districts, and applications for the 2026-27 school year are closed.
programs.what_children_do: Rake up a pile of leaves and play in it, then dig into how those leaves turn into soil. Learn to identify local trees through games, plant peas to take back to school, and become pollinators themselves in the spring. Every visit has an introduction, a snack break and a talking stick circle at the end, and the children build a circle journal across the year that becomes a poster on the last visit.
programs.our_note: This one is free but you have to apply, and the places for this school year have already gone. Only three adults may come with the class, counting the teacher, so plan your helpers around that number. Ask when applications open again, because dates for the whole year are set in early September.
programs.practical_summary: Mornings from 9:30 to noon, rain or shine, so the children need proper coats and boots. Washrooms on site are accessible and mostly private and gender neutral, and there are wheelchair accessible planters in the food garden.
programs.evidence: Each class is permitted to bring a maximum of three adults including the classroom teacher.

programs.name: Group visit to the gardens
programs.description: A self guided visit to the 70 acre garden and woodland at the published admission rates, with a discount for larger groups. Groups of 10 to 19 get 10% off admission, groups of 20 to 24 get 20% off, and groups of 25 or more get 25% off. Children aged 12 and under are free at any time and youth pay $5, $6 or $10 depending on the month. Between April and September there is a free public tour every Thursday and Friday from 1 pm to 2 pm starting at the Welcome Centre, included in the price of admission, and private tours can be requested by email for days they are already open. A Garden Discovery Backpack with journaling tools, bug and bird identification cards, two magnifying glasses and a free Plant Heroes journal for each child can be borrowed from the Welcome Centre until 3 pm, one backpack per family.
programs.what_children_do: Walk down the gravel, boardwalk and woodchip trails through the woodland to the gardens, the ponds and Milner House, looking at rhododendrons and towering old growth Douglas firs on the way.
programs.our_note: The property is a long gentle slope and the walk back up is the part that catches people out. A shuttle cart carrying six to eight people runs the driveway and will take a folded stroller or a walker on the back, so ask a staff member to call one rather than pushing everyone uphill. The discovery backpacks are lent one per family, so they will not stretch to a whole group.
programs.practical_summary: Accessible washrooms are at the Welcome Centre, the Pool House Gift Shop and Milner House, and three accessible parking stalls sit beside the Welcome Centre. Bus parking and an indoor place to eat are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Children aged 12 and under are free, but youth over 12 and adults pay admission, which changes with the month and ranges from $5 to $10 for youth and $7 to $14 for adults.
programs.evidence: Groups coming to visit the Gardens may receive a 10% discount of admission for groups of 10-19

gaps: PRICE IS PER GROUP, NOT PER CHILD, AND THIS IS A QUOTE NOT AN INFERENCE. The field trip page reads, word for word, "$200 per group. Maximum group size is one class, or 30 students for community groups." It was read again in a browser from the live page to be sure. Recorded per child instead, a class of 30 would have shown as $6,000 rather than $200.

The single visit field trip has no single age or grade range. Three of the five themes are written for all ages and two are written for grade 3 and up, so no age or grade range has been recorded for that program. The five visit program does publish grades, 1 to 7 with priority to 1 to 3.

youngest age welcomed is not stated anywhere. The field trip menu says all ages for three of its five themes and the site takes community groups, but nothing addresses toddlers or under threes specifically. Worth asking if your group is very young.

indoor lunch space is not stated. There is an indoor classroom space and a teaching shelter, both mentioned only in the accessibility notes, and the Camellia Tea Room is a paid restaurant. Nothing says where a class eats a packed lunch.
bus parking is not stated. The only parking detail published is three accessible stalls beside the Welcome Centre.
lead time for booking a field trip is not stated, and neither is a deposit, a payment method or a cancellation policy for the paid field trips.
The five visit program is free but applications for the 2026-27 school year are closed, and the site does not say when they open again.
Whether the $200 field trip fee includes tax is not stated.
Admission changes every month, so the adult figure recorded here is the September 2026 one. Children aged 12 and under are free in every month published.

The December entry on their winter page still lists the 2025 Milner Christmas Magic dates, so that season has already passed. Those evenings were admission by donation, which is neither free nor a price, so no cost has been recorded for them.

There is no Open Graph image on the site, and no published coordinates, no map embed and no location data block. The map in the footer is a flat picture with no coordinates in it, so the point here was worked out from the street address.
The site does not say what languages tours are given in.
The MAC Community Garden style workshops listed under Learn Here for master gardeners are aimed at adults, and the Garden Discovery Backpacks are lent one per family, so neither is a group offering.

conflicts.note: Their own pages give two different addresses for the person who runs the school programs, one short and one long form of the same name. If one bounces, try the other, or use the general garden address. Worth settling when you book.
